doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Abbey Lincoln and the Cedar Walton Trio at Wells in Harlem
summary: With Jack DeJohnette newly added, the trio backed Abbey Lincoln for a thirteen-week run at Wells in Harlem until a disco upstairs drowned out the music.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And gettin' with Abbey. Okay. So uh, uh, Mr. Moses on drums had to, had to go home on a family emergency; Jack DeJohnette was just arriving into New York from Chicago; and uh, we quickly groomed him for the trio behind Abbey Lincoln. Abbey Lincoln and the Cedar
Walton Trio. Must have been a thirteen week engagement at a place named Wells in Harlem. That's the home of Chicken and Waffles, yeah, uh …

Yeah, so uh, we stayed there a long time and then uh, with great success, I mean, it wasn't that big a place – along the lines of the size of the, the, the Bohemian Caverns, but totally different, you know, totally different. The bar was soon as you walked in the door, you know, the bar started.
That was down the street or up the street from Count Basie's. Wasn't Count Basie on the same [street?]?

Uh, Count Basie's was practically next door on the same side of the street. But uh, that was a wonderful gig – until they decided to put upstairs a disco, which would have been all right but in between our songs, you could hear Dum Dum Dum Dum.
Was that similar to your experience this weekend?
No, I didn't even know it was up there.
On the 3rd floor of the Caverns?
Okay, look, I hope you don't notice it tonight either.
Yeah, I'm sorry you brought it up because I, I, I certainly … We're so far from – aren't we? – where they are. They're not directly above the stage, are they?
Oh, two flights up. Yeah. I didn't hear them. But this is one flight up in, in, in Wells, and you could hear Dum Dum, and uh, Abbey said, "I can't take this, Cedar."
